value.text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to take another look at merging emergency dispatch. He pitched it as a way to save money as the city prepares for revenue losses under Amendment 3 . Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago. He said Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system, and he told council members his offer still stands. "I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system," Flowers said. He asked that it be considered "as a potential cost savings" as the city makes what he called "difficult decisions" under Amendment 3. Florida voters approved a ballot initiative that will slash non-school property taxes despite a campaign by local officials warning it would gut funding for public safety and other services. It will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Council member Tracey Zudans asked city staff to put numbers on the idea. "I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well," Zudans said. "I'd be happy to have my staff work with you guys," Flowers said. Mayor Aaron Vos said city staff will total what the city spends on dispatch now, and Flowers will bring back what it would cost the city to join a countywide call center. Vos said he expects a unified center would be run by the county, not the sheriff, similar to St. Lucie County's. Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether the dispatch center would be a county function or run by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. "I have the bulk of dispatchers that work for me at the sheriff's office, so I can only offer it from my side," Flowers said. "You would have to ask the county if they were interested in maybe doing it differently." He added that the sheriff's office and the county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship. See also: 22-year-old West Palm Beach motorcyclist struck, killed by SUV in Loxahatchee That relationship has been strained before. In July 2025 a budget debate erupted during an Indian River County Commission meeting, prompting the board to call a 15-minute recess after tensions flared between commissioners and Flowers. Flowers was requesting $93.5 million that year, while the county recommended a budget closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately voted to raise the sheriff's budget by $6.8 million, far less than he requested. Flowers later sued the commission , which then held a special meeting over the sheriff's budget. "This is a very deep issue," Flowers said. "If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together." Council members took no action on the proposal. Vos said Amendment 3 means the city has to consider every option. "With the implications of Amendment 3, we have to look at all aspects of where we can save money," Vos said. "If it saves us money, that's what we need to do." But Vos said moving dispatch out of the police department could come with a hidden cost. "You could lose some of that rapport between the call center staff and the officers due to familiarity," he said. Vos said he talked with police leaders in Sebastian and Fellsmere after Flowers first pitched the idea. He said Sebastian police used the sheriff's call center until 2007, then went back to running their own. Vero Beach Police Chief David Currey said his position on keeping the city's dispatch center has not changed. Vero Beach and Sebastian police are the only agencies in the county that run their own dispatch. "The dispatchers know the officers. They know the community members," Currey said. "If we don't have that under our umbrella, then I don't have control over any of that." Currey said the department switched to a new computer-aided dispatch and records management system in June. He said the department is working with the sheriff's office to connect the two agencies' dispatch systems, which would let dispatchers see where deputies and officers are and handle calls without transferring them. Currey said the idea last came up around 2012. He said the sheriff at the time told the city that dispatching for Vero Beach would likely cost about the same, if not more. "We have ten dispatchers, and they have salaries, and they have benefits," Currey said. "That will cost him just like it'll cost us." Despite the uncertainty around Amendment 3, Currey said the department is not freezing hiring and is interviewing for a police officer position now.

For some children, the biggest worry this holiday season should be who gets caught first in a game of hide-and-seek or who can throw a football the farthest.But for families facing housing insecurity, the reality can be much different.WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE HERE: For more than four decades, Adopt-A-Family of the Palm Beaches has worked to make sure families with children have a safe, stable place to call home.The nonprofit provides affordable and supportive housing for families experiencing homelessness or at risk of losing their homes. Its work also extends beyond housing, offering resources designed to help parents and children build long-term stability.At one of the organization's residential campuses, families live within walking distance of a playground, where children have a place to play while their parents work toward a more secure future."We are surrounded by 87 units of supportive housing which are located within a tenth of a mile of this playground," said Matt Constantine, CEO of Adopt-A-Family of the Palm Beaches.Constantine says the campus setting allows the organization to bring several services directly to the families it serves.Those resources include educational support for children, after-school programming, career coaching, case management and on-site mental health services.The goal is to address the challenges that can make it difficult for families to remain housed and financially independent."Provide housing stability to families with children who are either experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless," Constantine said, describing the organization's longstanding mission.But as housing costs continue to rise, the need for assistance is growing."Our phones ring all day long," Constantine said.He says the upfront cost of securing a rental property can be a significant obstacle for families already struggling financially."And the first, last, and security deposit comes out to almost eight thousand dollars, ten thousand dollars," he said.Children are also at the center of the organization's work. Constantine says roughly two-thirds of the people served by Adopt-A-Family are children, making educational and emotional support an important part of its mission."Two-thirds of who we serve are children, so a big responsibility that we have and a big component of the work we do is to be there for that next generation," Constantine said.Through United Way of Palm Beach County's Season of Hope campaign, Adopt-A-Family is among the local nonprofit agencies receiving community support to continue its work helping families in need.For Constantine, the effort is about more than providing assistance during the holidays. It's about neighbors stepping up for one another."I think that's the secret of building a healthy community. It's being there for your neighbor," he said.HOW TO HELP:Community members interested in supporting Adopt-A-Family of the Palm Beaches can learn more about its programs, make a donation or explore volunteer opportunities by visiting www.aafpbc.org.

Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, are in custody after the Martin County Sheriff's Office says a 17-year-old heard a suspicious noise outside his family's home in Palm City's Evergreen Club, prompting a 911 call and an extensive overnight search. Investigators say the group parked a vehicle near the C-23 Canal before walking into the gated community and targeting a home. Deputies later recovered masks, gloves and a stolen firearm during their investigation.WATCH: Teen's Alert Leads to 4 Arrests After Palm City ManhuntThe sheriff's office is now asking residents in the Evergreen Club community to check their homes, vehicles and security cameras for anything suspicious as investigators try to determine why the group traveled from Jacksonville to Martin County and whether any other properties were targeted.Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when the family's 17-year-old son realized something was wrong."The 17-year-old son heard a noise, woke up, knew something was wrong, but didn't quite know what it was," Budensiek said. "(He) went and talked to his parents."The family then began reviewing footage from security cameras around the property.According to Budensiek, one camera was no longer working properly. When the family went farther back through the recorded footage, he said they discovered people moving around the home."They could see that one of their cameras wasn't working," Budensiek said. "They kept going further back in their search history, and saw where these three black males actually were circling the house."Budensiek said the video showed someone placing a sticker over a camera lens near the back door so activity there could no longer be seen.The family called 911.Deputies began searching the area outside the gated community and checked a parking lot near the C-23 Canal."There indeed was a car parked there," Budensiek said.The sheriff's office said the suspects had parked along the canal before walking into the neighborhood.One person was taken into custody near the vehicle, while the others fled, according to the sheriff.Deputies established a perimeter and searched with assistance from aviation and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department. Budensiek said two of the people who fled were ultimately discovered hiding beneath the bridge carrying Murphy Road over the C-23 Canal."Two fled and ended up hiding under the bridge that crosses the C-23 Canal on Murphy Road," Budensiek said. "They were the last two to actually be apprehended after an extensive manhunt."The three adults arrested were identified as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A 16-year-old was also arrested, but WPTV is not identifying the juvenile.All four face attempted home invasion charges, according to published reports citing the sheriff's office. Wise also faces grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. As investigators retraced the route between the suspects' vehicle and the family's home, Budensiek said they recovered a handgun."They recovered a handgun that was stolen with an extended magazine, and were able to corroborate again what the intended victim said," Budensiek said.The Sheriff's Office has also reported recovering masks and gloves during the investigation. Investigators are now trying to determine why this particular home may have been targeted."We don't know why that house," Budensiek said. "We don't know if they went to any other houses potentially in the middle of the night."The sheriff's office is asking residents to review their security footage and inspect their homes and vehicles for missing property or possible evidence of another attempted break-in.Anyone who discovers missing property or signs of a break-in is asked to contact the Martin County Sheriff's Office at 772-220-7060.Investigators are also examining digital evidence as they work to establish why the four made the trip from Jacksonville to Palm City.MORE PALM CITY: Judge rejects motion to dismiss animal cruelty case against Palm City dog trainer Nikki CamerlengoThis story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. With Thanksgiving approaching, West Palm Beach police officers are helping make sure local families and individuals have a meal for the holiday.THE FUND, a nonprofit that supports the West Palm Beach Police Department, provided 150 Thanksgiving meals for officers to deliver to residents in need across the city.WATCH REPORT BELOW: Officers loaded the meals into police vehicles Tuesday morning at Heart and Soul Park on North Rosemary Avenue before taking them directly to residents' homes.According to organizers, police officers identified the families and individuals who could use additional support during the holiday season.The effort is a collaboration between THE FUND and the West Palm Beach Police Department.THE FUND is a nonprofit organization that works to supplement resources for the police department beyond what is available through the city's budget. The organization says its broader mission is to support officers while helping improve public safety and quality of life in West Palm Beach.

People across South Florida and the Treasure Coast are bracing for yet another round of heavy rain, and one Indian River County community is pleading for help after battling repeated flooding this month.Joe Waters documented his frustration Saturday evening, recording on his phone in front of his mobile home in the Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach as a car drove through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights.WATCH REPORT BELOW: Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them."The water came up probably about thigh high," Waters said. "Came up into the driveway, went into the house."Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company.When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered — fed up after battling multiple floods just this month.Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, told me she wants to be a voice for her neighbors, especially those who can't speak up."They just want to feel safe in their homes," she said.The flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders, Carboni said."We had a gentleman who needed EMS to come out, and they could not get to his home, so they had to park out on 82nd (Avenue), and then a large fire truck had to get to the home," Carboni said.With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened."People are afraid. It's horrible living in fear when you don't know if it's going to rain and you're going to be able to leave your home the next day."She wants to spread awareness about what her community is going through."We need help, and we're asking for help," Carboni said.Emergency managers in Indian River County tell me they're operating at a Level 2 emergency, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. They've extended the state of emergency through Sunday, Nov. 30.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

A St. Lucie County woman, who had told investigators she was trying to exorcise demons from her son's body, has been declared unfit to stand trial in his death.Court records show that Rhonda Paulynice was committed to the Department of Children and Families to see if her competency can be restored. WATCH REPORT BELOW: St. Lucie County mother unfit for trial in son's deathIn May 2025, school resource deputies requested a welfare check after the boy, 6-year-old Ra'myl Pierre, had been out of school for several days.The boy's body was found on a bed wrapped in fabric with only his face exposed.According to a probable cause affidavit, Paulynice told deputies she suffocated her son 12 days before his body was found inside the Fort Pierce area home they shared.

Thanksgiving came with a little extra help for families in Delray Beach as local high school students teamed up with police officers to make sure they had a holiday meal on the table.Students from Atlantic High School’s Criminal Justice Academy partnered with the Delray Beach Police Department to deliver more than a dozen full Thanksgiving meals to families in need across the city.WATCH: Atlantic High School students, Delray Beach police deliver Thanksgiving meals to families in needFor the students, the annual effort is about more than dropping off food. It’s an opportunity to learn what it means to serve the community beyond the classroom.“It teaches you to be less selfish and care more about what is going on around you and how you can help,” student Alexis Felicetta said.The students went door to door alongside Delray Beach police officers, personally delivering the meals and meeting the families receiving them.“We are helping families, and seeing them smile when they open the door makes me happy,” student Micaja Paul Joseph said.The Thanksgiving meal giveaway has become a tradition for the Criminal Justice Academy and Delray Beach police, continuing for more than decade.Major Gary Ferreri with the Delray Beach Police Department said the experience also gives students perspective on hardships other people in their community may be facing.“Some of the kids come from tough situations. They get to see that even as bad as they have it, there are others that have it tougher sometimes.”For one family, the delivery meant being able to have a Thanksgiving turkey without worrying about how to pay for it.“We didn't really have money to buy a turkey for Thanksgiving,” a family member said. “For me, it's happy because I get to spend more time with my family.”For the students, police officers and families taking part, the tradition is proving a little help can go a long way.

A Port St. Lucie man has been sentenced to nearly four years in federal prison for using artificial intelligence to impersonate a popular online streamer as part of a cryptocurrency fraud scheme that authorities say cost victims about $260,000.David Anthony Sanchez, 36, was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida.Federal prosecutors said Sanchez, who also went by "Dave the Jewler," "Rueben Alexis De Jesus Santana" and other aliases, impersonated online streamer N3ON to convince organizers of a cryptocurrency memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse and participate in it.According to court records, Sanchez created online accounts designed to look as though they belonged to N3ON and communicated with the project's organizers while posing as both the streamer and his representative.Prosecutors said Sanchez also executed agreements using N3ON's identity and sent organizers an AI-generated voice recording that mimicked the streamer's voice to falsely confirm his participation.Believing the representations were legitimate, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts controlled by Sanchez, according to prosecutors.Authorities said Sanchez later converted a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to conceal the source and ownership of the money. Prosecutors said he used the proceeds for his personal benefit."Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said in the release. She said Sanchez exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate victims' trust and take their money.In addition to his 47-month prison sentence, Sanchez was ordered to pay restitution to the victims. The amount of restitution was not specified in the release.The FBI's Miami Field Office investigated the case.

St. Lucie County commissioners are scheduled to consider adopting the final draft of the 2026 Port of Fort Pierce Master Plan during their Dec. 1 meeting. County Port, Inlet and Beaches staff will present the plan at the meeting, which begins at 6 p.m. Commissioners can ask questions and approve the document as presented or amend it before adoption, according to the county. The update builds on the port’s 2020 master plan and incorporates feedback from residents and industry stakeholders since commissioners last reviewed the draft on Aug. 11. The plan is intended to guide future development and help the county seek state and federal grants for port improvements. Among the long-term opportunities in the draft is a Launch Vehicle Recovery Facility to support offshore rocket recovery operations, including drone ships and other support vessels. As CBS12 previously reported, the proposed facility could position Fort Pierce to support recovery work tied to Florida’s growing space industry . The plan describes it as one part of a broader working waterfront vision, alongside mega-yacht services, marine research and workforce training, recreation and public access. The rocket-recovery proposal is one part of a broader vision for the Port of Fort Pierce as a mixed-use working waterfront. The plan also outlines Harbour Pointe as a public-facing district, with a regional boat ramp, waterfront dining and commercial space, an entertainment pavilion, a shared-use path and a living shoreline. The update also envisions a marine research and workforce training campus focused on marine science, environmental education and training for waterfront jobs. It calls for continued growth of the port’s mega-yacht maintenance and repair operations, as well as a marina at Museum Pointe where yachts could dock temporarily for crew changes, provisioning or staging before service. The plan includes infrastructure and access projects, such as a new road to Harbour Pointe, stormwater improvements and a possible connection to the regional Sun Trail. It also proposes a future Port to Park link to improve access between the waterfront and Franklin Park. See also: 3 auto insurers directed to refund $122 million in excess profits to Florida customers The 2026 update supplements the port’s 2020 master plan rather than replacing it. The document lays out a long-term vision for development; proposed zoning changes and the Port Overlay District remain under discussion. The county says commissioners will consider the plan during their regular meeting in the Commission Chambers on the third floor of the Roger Poitras Administration Annex, 2300 Virginia Ave. in Fort Pierce. The meeting will also be streamed on the county’s website and YouTube channel. Residents can review the draft plan on the county’s Port Master Plan webpage .

What is the best golf course in America?Golf.com broke down the top 100 courses, which they call a "Top 100 Courses in the U.S. for 2026-27: The ultimate bucket list for American golf".So, how do they determine the list? It's a democratic vote with the panelists.Golf.com said each panelist gets a ballot with hundreds of courses. Beside the list of courses are 11 groupings. If a panelist considers a course to be among the top three in the U.S., they tick the first column. If they believe the course to be among Nos. 4-10, they check that column, followed by 11-25 and so on. They even have a column for “remove.” The organization is also careful with panelist selections to include a variety of input and to avoid anyone with ties to any of the courses.Research shows golf is experiencing a resurgence as a hobby. The National Golf Foundation reports that 30.6 million Americans play golf, that's up 1.7 million from the previous year and a new record.Did any Florida courses make the list?Course: TPC Sawgrass (Players Stadium), Ponte Vedra BeachRank: 53Built: 1981Designer: Pete DyeCourse: Seminole, Juno BeachRank: 17Built: 1926Designer: Donald Ross

A homeowner's quick call to 911 helped interrupt an attempted home invasion in Palm City early Tuesday, leading to the arrests of four people from Jacksonville, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.The sheriff's office said the homeowner heard a noise outside a home on Southwest Bimini Circle in the Evergreen Club and contacted authorities. Investigators said at least one of the suspects was armed with a handgun.When deputies arrived, the four suspects scattered into the neighborhood, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies established a perimeter and, with assistance from the agency's aviation, drone and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department K-9 unit, found all four hiding in separate locations throughout the community.Investigators believe the group parked near a canal and walked into the neighborhood to target the home. Deputies said they recovered a firearm, masks and gloves. Detectives later determined the gun had been reported stolen.The sheriff's office identified three of those arrested as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. The fourth person arrested is 16 years old. WPTV is not naming the juvenile.All four face attempted home invasion charges and were taken into custody, according to the sheriff's office.Wise also faces charges of grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.The sheriff's office credited the homeowner's quick decision to call authorities with interrupting the alleged crime before anyone was hurt.

A 19-year-old woman escaped with minor injuries after police say a man armed with a knife forced her into a wooded area along Boca Raton’s El Rio Trail and attempted to sexually assault her Monday morning.Boca Raton police said 36-year-old LaPaul Jackson was arrested a short time later aboard a public bus as he allegedly tried to leave the area.WATCH REPORT BELOW:Officers responded shortly after 11:30 a.m. to a report of an assault along the El Rio Trail, just north of Spanish River Boulevard.According to police, the woman was walking along the trail when a man she did not know approached her from behind with a knife. Investigators said he forced her into a nearby wooded area where a small camp had been set up.Police said the man attempted to sexually assault the woman and committed additional lewd acts before she was able to escape and run back toward the trail. Another person then called police.The woman suffered minor injuries and gave officers a detailed description of the suspect, police said.Officers established a perimeter and worked with the woman to track her cellphone, which police said the suspect had taken. Real-time location information showed the phone was moving, leading investigators to believe the suspect had boarded a public bus.Officers stopped the bus near North Federal Highway and Northeast 20th Street. Police said they identified Jackson aboard the bus and recovered the woman's cellphone.Jackson was arrested on charges of armed kidnapping, armed robbery and attempted sexual battery. Police said additional charges are pending.He was later taken to the Palm Beach County Jail.The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact Boca Raton police Detective Gannon at 561-620-6073.

A homeowner in Palm City helped foil an attempted home invasion that occurred at the Evergreen Club. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says on Tuesday morning a homeowner on SW Bimini Circle heard a noise outside of their home, leading them to call 911 and interrupting the home invasion. When deputies arrived at the scene, the four suspects, three men and a teenager from Jacksonville, scattered into the neighborhood. The sheriff's office says deputies set up a perimeter around the neighborhood with help from its aviation team, K-9 unit, and the Stuart Police Department. K9's were able to track down all four suspects hiding in separate locations throughout the community. The sheriff's office says at least one of the suspects was armed. Further investigation revealed that the suspects parked along the canal and walked into the neighborhood to target the home. The sheriff's office says during the apprehension they uncovered masks, a firearm and gloves. The suspects were identified as: Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 21 Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21 Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21 Teenage boy, 16 All four were charged with an attempted home invasion and were taken to the Martin County Jail. Wise faces an additional charge of grand theft and possession of a firearm. See also: Boca Raton police arrest man after reported assault on El Rio Trail The agency is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. Anyone who finds anything missing should call the sheriff’s office at 772-220-7060. This is a developing news story.

The Martin County Sheriff’s Office , along with Florida Highway Patrol, are investigating a serious crash involving a vehicle and a tractor-trailer. MCSO says a serious injury crash involving a vehicle and tractor-trailer occurred on Monday at U.S. 1 at SE Hobe Terrace in Hobe Sound. Martin County Fire Rescue’s LifeStar flew one person with life-threatening injuries to St. Mary’s Medical Center, MCSO said. A second person was also injured in the crash. See also: Boynton Beach police arrest man on fentanyl, cocaine trafficking charges This is a developing story, check back for updates.

Several organizations across the Treasure Coast are offering free food distributions, grocery giveaways and prepared Thanksgiving meals this week to help residents in need ahead of the holiday. The distributions are taking place Nov. 23-26 in Fort Pierce, Port St. Lucie, Indiantown and Sebastian. Participating locations include local churches, food ministries and community organizations. Available assistance includes groceries, holiday food and prepared meals, with distribution times and offerings varying by location. Some distributions will continue while supplies last. Residents are encouraged to contact individual organizations before traveling to confirm availability, eligibility requirements and distribution details. A Port St. Lucie family is remembering their 24-year-old daughter after she was killed in a hit-and-run last week. Alexis Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was riding her scooter to work on Nov. 16 when she was struck by a vehicle near SW Gatlin Boulevard, according to police. She died the following day, Nov. 17. For the first time, her father and relatives are sharing memories of the young woman they say brought joy to everyone around her. Alexis wasn't just a ray of sunshine, you know. I think to us she was just the sun, her father, Alberto Vasquez, said As the eldest daughter, Vasquez said Alexis had a natural instinct to care for others, beginning with her own siblings. Ever since she was born she just, she had a passion for caring for others, starting with her siblings, you know, he said. At the family's Port St. Lucie home, Vasquez and relatives, some visiting from Texas, gathered around photos of Alexis as they remembered her life. She was the sweetest person ever, and it's a huge loss for the family, her aunt, Minerva Benitez, said. Also read: Port St. Lucie hit-and-run victim dies; driver could face more serious charges Vasquez said the support they have received has helped them. It's really helped us get through these first difficult days that were unbearable, he said. He remembered his daughter as someone who loved children and dreamed of working with them. He was also proud of her time in Junior ROTC. On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched Alexis leave home for her job at Wendy's. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He said he saw her riding away on her scooter and assumed she would be OK. Five minutes later, he learned there had been a crash. Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer in connection with the crash. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. He's accused of hitting Cuellar as she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving the scene. He is currently charged with leaving the scene. Additional charges, including vehicular homicide, could follow. Vasquez said he wishes he could have been there to help his daughter. I'm sorry that I couldn't be there for her, maybe help her. And that I loved her deeply because I didn't get a chance to tell her that, he said. Now, he is preparing a place at home where he plans to bring her. A service for Alexis will be held Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce. Police are continuing to investigate the crash.

Two men are facing felony burglary charges after allegedly breaking into a Hutchinson Island business to play video games after hours, the Martin County Sheriff's Office said. The incident occurred late Saturday into early Sunday morning at the Indian River Plantation Shopping Plaza, according to Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek. A security guard on patrol noticed something unusual and called 911. "He happens upon an individual that had the back door of a restaurant/bowling alley game room, and as he tried to confront that individual, he fled," Budensiek said. Footage from the sheriff's Air One unit showed deputies tracking a suspect from above. "He should be coming up on your right side. Stop, stop the car," a deputy said in the video. Deputies located one man walking down the road and another emerging from the woods with an electric scooter. "Facedown, facedown, all the way down," a deputy said during the arrest. The sheriff said the suspects were identified as 29-year-old Ferdinand Schoedinger IV of New Hampshire and 33-year-old James Bolon of Ohio. Both men were reportedly placed at Local Lanes Duckpin Bowling and Eatery on Hutchinson Island. The sheriff said one of the suspects admitted they broke into the business because they wanted to play video games after it had closed. "They had been there earlier, had enjoyed it, were trying to come back and continue playing Pac-Man. And ended up in a serious game of hide-and-go-seek with the Martin County Sheriff's Office," Budensiek said. Budensiek also issued a warning to visitors. "Don't come here and do stupid things; definitely don't come here and try to victimize our citizens," he said. Both suspects have bonded out but face felony burglary charges. Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, are in custody after the Martin County Sheriff's Office says a 17-year-old heard a suspicious noise outside his family's home in Palm City's Evergreen Club, prompting a 911 call and an extensive overnight search. Investigators say the group parked a vehicle near the C-23 Canal before walking into the gated community and targeting a home. Deputies later recovered masks, gloves and a stolen firearm during their investigation. WATCH: Teen's Alert Leads to 4 Arrests After Palm City Manhunt The sheriff's office is now asking residents in the Evergreen Club community to check their homes, vehicles and security cameras for anything suspicious as investigators try to determine why the group traveled from Jacksonville to Martin County and whether any other properties were targeted. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when the family's 17-year-old son realized something was wrong. "The 17-year-old son heard a noise, woke up, knew something was wrong, but didn't quite know what it was," Budensiek said. "(He) went and talked to his parents." The family then began reviewing footage from security cameras around the property. According to Budensiek, one camera was no longer working properly. When the family went farther back through the recorded footage, he said they discovered people moving around the home. "They could see that one of their cameras wasn't working," Budensiek said. "They kept going further back in their search history, and saw where these three black males actually were circling the house." Budensiek said the video showed someone placing a sticker over a camera lens near the back door so activity there could no longer be seen. Deputies began searching the area outside the gated community and checked a parking lot near the C-23 Canal. "There indeed was a car parked there," Budensiek said. The sheriff's office said the suspects had parked along the canal before walking into the neighborhood. One person was taken into custody near the vehicle, while the others fled, according to the sheriff. Deputies established a perimeter and searched with assistance from aviation and K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department. Budensiek said two of the people who fled were ultimately discovered hiding beneath the bridge carrying Murphy Road over the C-23 Canal. "Two fled and ended up hiding under the bridge that crosses the C-23 Canal on Murphy Road," Budensiek said. "They were the last two to actually be apprehended after an extensive manhunt." The three adults arrested were identified as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A 16-year-old was also arrested, but WPTV is not identifying the juvenile. All four face attempted home invasion charges, according to published reports citing the sheriff's office. Wise also faces grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. As investigators retraced the route between the suspects' vehicle and the family's home, Budensiek said they recovered a handgun. "They recovered a handgun that was stolen with an extended magazine, and were able to corroborate again what the intended victim said," Budensiek said. The Sheriff's Office has also reported recovering masks and gloves during the investigation. Investigators are now trying to determine why this particular home may have been targeted. "We don't know why that house," Budensiek said. "We don't know if they went to any other houses potentially in the middle of the night." The sheriff's office is asking residents to review their security footage and inspect their homes and vehicles for missing property or possible evidence of another attempted break-in. Anyone who discovers missing property or signs of a break-in is asked to contact the Martin County Sheriff's Office at 772-220-7060. Investigators are also examining digital evidence as they work to establish why the four made the trip from Jacksonville to Palm City. One person was killed and another suffered life-threatening injuries in a four-vehicle crash near Interstate 95 in Riviera Beach early Sunday morning, police said.The Riviera Beach Police Department said officers and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue responded to the intersection of West Blue Heron Boulevard and I-95 around 5:32 a.m. after the city's communications center received multiple 911 calls reporting a crash.Police said investigators determined that a 2022 Nissan Altima exited the northbound I-95 ramp and continued across the median, striking a 2021 Acura ILX that was stopped at a red light while facing west and waiting to turn onto southbound I-95.The initial impact led to a chain-reaction crash involving two other vehicles, according to police.The driver of the Acura was pronounced dead at the scene. A 26-year-old passenger had to be extricated from the vehicle and was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries.Police said the driver and passenger of the Nissan were also taken to a hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening.The names of those involved have not been released pending notification of their families.The Riviera Beach Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit is investigating the crash. Police said criminal charges are pending.Anyone with information about the crash is asked to contact Riviera Beach police at 561-845-4123.

Cleanup crews and residents are continuing to clear damage left behind by an EF-1 tornado that tore through southern Palm Beach County on Saturday evening, toppling trees and damaging homes, vehicles and other property from west Boca Raton through west Delray Beach.WATCH: EF-1 tornado cleanup continues in Delray BeachThe National Weather Service said the tornado reached peak winds of 102 mph and traveled 7.64 miles after first touching down around 6:04 p.m. near Boca Gardens. WPTV crews surveying damage in the Delray Beach area found a massive tree that came crashing down and crushed a stone wall. "It was pretty rumbling when it came through, and I rushed my wife into the bathroom, and it only lasted about a minute."Symia said he had never experienced a tornado before and worries he did not initially react quickly enough."I kind of think I reacted late because it all started prior to me getting her into the bathroom," he said.When Symia stepped outside the following morning, he could see just how much had changed around his home."The tree was coming through there, and it ended up over here," he said. "You couldn't get through here. You had to drive around, and there was another two or three trees down here."The damage was widespread along the tornado's path. Three weeks after historic flooding damaged and destroyed homes in Riviera Beach's Lone Pine community, residents are still gutting houses, searching for materials and relying on volunteers as they try to rebuild. Now, Mayor Douglas Lawson says the city is launching Rebuild Lone Pine Together, a community-driven initiative aimed at getting money, manpower and other resources to families who need help immediately.WPTV reporter Michael Hoffman was in Lone Pine the night of the flooding and returned to the neighborhood weeks later.WATCH: Riviera Beach launches effort to rebuild Lone PineThe water is gone, but signs of the destruction remain throughout the community. Dumpsters line streets outside gutted homes as families work to rebuild their lives heading into the holiday season.Inside one of those damaged homes, Hoffman met Edward Carr.Carr doesn't live in Lone Pine. He answered a call for volunteers after historic rainfall devastated the neighborhood."They said they needed some drywall, like replaced because they had flooding," Carr said. "So as you can see, I started pulling off the baseboards."The family living in the home invited WPTV inside but asked to remain anonymous.That's also where Hoffman met Denise Smith, another Lone Pine resident."We need a lot of hands because many hands make light work," Smith said. "It's what my grandmother used to say."Smith's own home down the street was destroyed by the flooding. She showed WPTV images of the damage.Despite being displaced herself, she was helping someone else rebuild.For Smith and Carr, two needs stand out across Lone Pine: volunteers and building materials."Right now is the time for Riviera Beach to come together as one community," Lawson said.Hoffman walked through Lone Pine with Lawson as they discussed what comes next for families who cannot afford to wait.Lawson said the city is working to bring together $2 million in available funding. But he also acknowledged that accessing money can involve bureaucratic hurdles, while residents need help now.That's where Rebuild Lone Pine Together comes in."It's really driven and led by the community," Lawson said. "It's focused on community advocates, leaders, nonprofits to come together with the resources, the funding, the dollars, the manpower."The effort is designed to bring together organizations, volunteers and other partners capable of filling immediate needs as residents continue working to recover.Lawson said the call for assistance goes far beyond Riviera Beach."We're calling across this country; we're saying we need support here in Riviera Beach and Lone Pine," Lawson said. "We're asking all our shareholders, all our partners, everybody just has an interest in supporting people to come provide support."Hoffman took the mayor's plan back to Smith and Carr.Smith described herself as "optimistically hopeful."But three weeks after the flooding, she also wants to see assistance reach residents faster."I'm the glass half full kind of person, but it's, you know, it's been three weeks, and I know there's a process," Smith said. "So I just hope that the wheels can start to turn a little bit faster, because people are displaced. I'm displaced, and people really don't have places to go."For families approaching the holidays with damaged homes and uncertain living arrangements, the launch of Rebuild Lone Pine Together represents another potential path toward recovery.But the work is only beginning.WPTV will continue tracking the initiative, including whether the promised resources, volunteers and funding make their way to the families still rebuilding in Lone Pine.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. The holiday rush to the airport for Thanksgiving is underway, and passengers are paying more this year to fly.According to AAA, the average domestic round-trip flight is costing $800. That figure is up 17% from a year ago, largely because of jet fuel costs.WATCH REPORT BELOW: "We've seen increases this year anywhere between 20 and 30%," said Clint Henderson at The Points Guy website. "My fear is, the CEOs are basically getting used to these higher costs, and they've suggested that even if the cost of jet fuel drops, they may not lower prices that much."Henderson suggests that any last-minute holiday travelers should try booking a flight on the actual holiday to save some money.Also, it helps to be flexible when choosing a flight."I would have liked the 6 a.m. flight, but that was too expensive," said Karen Galitto, who was flying from West Palm Beach to Long Island on Monday.Another issue facing passengers is delays.Recently, computer and operational issues caused travel trouble, including this month's national ground stop and Sunday's issue that impacted Delta's weight and balance system."The reason they're delaying and canceling flights is out of an abundance of caution," Henderson said. Nearly 1.8 million chickens will be depopulated after highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly known as bird flu, was detected at a Cal-Maine Foods facility in Okeechobee County.Cal-Maine Foods announced Nov. 18 that the facility tested positive for highly pathogenic avian influenza, or HPAI. The company said the outbreak will lead to the depopulation of approximately 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, representing about 2.7% of the company's total flock.WATCH REPORT BELOW: Production at the Okeechobee County facility has temporarily stopped while Cal-Maine follows protocols established by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services has established a quarantine area following the detection, according to St. Lucie County government.The poultry quarantine extends from Okeechobee County into a rural portion of western St. Lucie County north of State Road 70 near the county line.People who own or care for poultry within the affected area are being advised to review the state's quarantine restrictions, which include limits on moving poultry and poultry products without FDACS authorization. Residents can check whether they are within the affected area using the state's interactive quarantine map.Cal-Maine said it is coordinating production and distribution among its other facilities in an effort to maintain its egg supply and minimize disruptions for customers.The company also said it maintains biosecurity programs at its facilities but noted that no farm is immune to HPAI. The virus remains present among wild birds, and the risk of outbreaks can increase during bird migration seasons.Health officials say the detection does not mean consumers should stop eating eggs. According to information provided by the company, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention considers the health risk from HPAI viruses to the general U.S. public to be low.The USDA also says HPAI is not transmitted through properly handled and cooked eggs. Cal-Maine said there is no known HPAI risk associated with eggs currently on the market and that no eggs have been recalled because of the outbreak.Cal-Maine said it is working with federal, state and local officials as it responds to the outbreak and works to reduce the risk of additional infections.The company said it expects to provide more information in its next quarterly report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission and does not anticipate providing interim updates unless information is considered material.Anyone with questions about the quarantine can contact FDACS at 850-410-0900 or find additional information through its Division of Animal Industry.

The sound of bagpipes and taps filled the air Saturday as the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office unveiled a new memorial honoring two deputies killed in the line of duty.The memorial, located outside the sheriff’s office’s new administration building, honors Sgt. Terri Sweeting-Mashkow and Cpl. Their deaths happened 40 years apart. Now, their names have a permanent place together.WATCH: New memorial honors two Indian River County deputies killed in line of dutyThe unveiling came exactly one year after Sweeting-Mashkow was killed while serving an eviction notice at a home in the Bermuda Club community.47-year-old Sweeting-Mashkow was one of three deputies serving the eviction notice on Nov. 21, 2025, when authorities said 37-year-old Michael Halberstam retrieved a weapon and opened fire. Sweeting-Mashkow was killed, and Deputy Florentino Arizpe was shot in the shoulder.A locksmith who was there for the eviction, David Long, was also critically wounded and later died from his injuries.Sweeting-Mashkow had served with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office for more than 25 years. Her death marked the second line-of-duty death in the 100-year history of the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.For those who gathered Saturday, the passage of a year has not made that loss feel distant.“It’s an honor to be out here but also very sad,” community member Joanne Knott said. “To think that it happened a year ago is strange because it feels like it was yesterday.”The memorial also reaches back four decades, honoring Cpl. Richard Raczkoski, who was killed in the line of duty 40 years ago.“The two heroes that are on this memorial are two people that our community will remember forever,” Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said.Hundreds of family members, friends, law enforcement officers and community members gathered for Saturday’s unveiling, paying their respects.“I am so glad that they did this for Terri and Raczkoski,” one community member said.For those at the ceremony, the memorial is also a reminder of the risks law enforcement officers face each time they go to work.“All of these officers that step out into the community, they never know what their day is going to bring,” says Knott.Flowers hopes the two names on the memorial will be the only ones it ever bears: “I hope we never have to add names to this memorial again."

People across South Florida and the Treasure Coast are bracing for yet another round of heavy rain , and one Indian River County community is pleading for help after battling repeated flooding this month. Joe Waters documented his frustration Saturday evening, recording on his phone in front of his mobile home in the Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach as a car drove through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights. Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company. When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered — fed up after battling multiple floods just this month. Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, told me she wants to be a voice for her neighbors, especially those who can’t speak up. “They just want to feel safe in their homes,” she said. The flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders, Carboni said. “We had a gentleman who needed EMS to come out, and they could not get to his home, so they had to park out on 82nd (Avenue), and then a large fire truck had to get to the home,” Carboni said. With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened. It’s horrible living in fear when you don’t know if it’s going to rain and you’re going to be able to leave your home the next day.” She wants to spread awareness about what her community is going through. “We need help, and we’re asking for help,” Carboni said. Emergency managers in Indian River County tell me they’re operating at a Level 2 emergency, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. They’ve extended the state of emergency through Sunday, Nov. 30. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. A new holiday tradition is taking root at the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, where Luminary Nights will bring holiday lights, nighttime lighthouse climbs, local music and shopping to the historic waterfront property in December.The limited event is scheduled for Dec. 11, 12, 18, and 19. Organizers say they are starting small this year with hopes of growing Luminary Nights into an annual family tradition in northern Palm Beach County."We really hope to make this a new family-friendly holiday tradition here in North County," Executive Director Katrina Heller said.A Banyan tree (ficus) that dances to musicOne of the most visual additions will be the Lighthouse's illuminated Banyan tree.Organizers have nicknamed it the "Dancing Tree" because its lights have been synchronized to music."We have lit it up and timed it to music, so we're calling it our dancing tree, and we'll have a new program every half hour," Heller said.Luminary Nights will also feature nighttime lighthouse climbs, holiday shopping, live music and a Kids Zone for families.Lighthouse climbs are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. Children must be at least 48 inches tall to climb.Tickets are $30 for adults and $20 for children. A family ticket for two adults and two children is $75.Keeping the holiday celebration localEvent Manager Simone Incendy said organizers are intentionally incorporating local businesses and musicians into Luminary Nights.The Vendor Village will feature local artists and small businesses, including vendors whose products are carried in the Lighthouse gift shop.Incendy said area high school bands and community bands will also be among the performers.The approach connects the new celebration to the community surrounding the landmark while giving small businesses and local performers another place to reach visitors during the holiday season.Proceeds from the event will go toward preserving the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, its history and its educational programming, according to event information provided by organizers.A new view of the Jupiter Inlet LighthouseThe holiday celebration isn't the only new attraction visitors will find at the Lighthouse.Heller said a shoreline restoration project is wrapping up with a grand opening scheduled for Dec. 3 at 1 p.m.The work includes a new seawall and a boardwalk stretching more than 800 feet around the point where the Loxahatchee River and Indian River meet."We're so excited for our new boardwalk," Heller said.She said the boardwalk will give visitors a new perspective of the Lighthouse property and the surrounding water, including opportunities to see fish below.For a landmark built around a light that has guided the Jupiter waterfront for generations, the additions bring together its past and future: a restored shoreline and new waterfront experience alongside a holiday celebration organizers hope families will return to year after year.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Hundreds of Palm Beach County families will have a complete Thanksgiving dinner on the table this year through Extraordinary Charities' Turkey Takeaway in West Palm Beach.Extraordinary Charities Executive Director Christine Raymond said the organization is providing fully prepared Thanksgiving meals to 400 families across Palm Beach County. Every available meal has already been claimed, and the organization has filled its volunteer needs.Now, Raymond said, the final need is financial support from the community.“This Thanksgiving we're feeding 400 families across Palm Beach County with a fully prepared Thanksgiving meal,” Raymond said. “All of those meals have been claimed. We're all good with our volunteers, and now the last remaining piece is to gather some community financial support because it costs us about $50 per family to feed them.”CLICK HERE to donate.What's inside a Turkey Takeaway meal?For the families receiving the meals, Thanksgiving comes with all the familiar favorites.Ashleigh McDonald with Extraordinary Charities said each meal includes green beans, gravy, cranberry sauce, stuffing, mashed potatoes, pumpkin pie, and a fully cooked turkey.The meals are scheduled for pickup Nov. 24 and 25.The organization's registration information also offered families the opportunity to request diapers by size with their meals.A change of plans in the kitchenPreparing hundreds of Thanksgiving dinners requires plenty of work, and this year's weather forced an adjustment.Chef Greg Schiff said rain meant the team couldn't prepare all the turkeys using its smoker as planned. Still, the kitchen crew kept the operation moving.“We're still getting the job done,” Schiff said. “I have great staff over here, supporting staff with Ms. Shiel, great crew, so everything is worthwhile knowing how it's going to feed people.”The work extended beyond the turkeys.Recipes for Success graduate Ronin Nance was helping portion stuffing into 20-ounce containers, repeating the process meal after meal.“Repetition is the key to learning,” Nance said.Giving families more than a mealExtraordinary Charities board member Cassius Johnson said the families being served are neighbors dealing with the pressure of rising costs.For Johnson, putting food on the table gives families an opportunity to continue a Thanksgiving tradition centered on togetherness.“This is our opportunity to give them the food that's around that table so they can continue with an amazing tradition,” Johnson said. “One of my favorite holidays where we can just give gratitude and give thanks and spark of joy among ourselves.”And even members of the board are part of the hands-on effort. Johnson spent part of the preparation working on cranberry sauce.With all 400 meals claimed and volunteer needs filled, Extraordinary Charities says financial contributions are the remaining way for people to support this year's Turkey Takeaway. Raymond said it costs the organization about $50 to provide a Thanksgiving meal for a family.At a time when household budgets can make a holiday meal more difficult to afford, hundreds of Palm Beach County families will still get a chance to gather around a Thanksgiving dinner, thanks to a community effort underway in West Palm Beach.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Hundreds of Palm Beach County families are getting help putting Thanksgiving dinner on the table through SPECTRA, the nonprofit arm of the Palm Beach County Housing Authority, as community partners work to address food insecurity during the holiday season.SPECTRA recently helped distribute 300 frozen turkeys and is now preparing Thanksgiving fixings for families in South Bay, according to Naderge Alcime, ROSS coordinator with the Palm Beach County Housing Authority.WATCH REPORT BELOW:The assistance comes as the Housing Authority says more than 280 additional families are on its waiting list for help.Filling needs beyond housingSPECTRA was created to help address needs that extend beyond putting a roof over someone's head."SPECTRA is our not-for-profit arm of the Housing Authority," Chief Financial Officer Tad Fuller said. "The Housing Authority, of course, houses individuals and families within our county. SPECTRA's job is to fill in those missing middle pieces."Fuller said those needs can include food, transportation and other services for residents.For some families, food insecurity can mean making difficult choices between basic necessities."A lot of our families are having issues with having enough food in their homes, and so having to choose between paying a light bill and or paying for childcare or buying food for Thanksgiving is a tough decision," Alcime said.300 turkeys and more help for South BayAlcime said SPECTRA recently completed a giveaway of 300 frozen turkeys and is continuing its Thanksgiving efforts in South Bay."We just did a 300 turkey giveaway last week, and now we're going to be going to South Bay to our new South Bay property and handing out, uh, these lovely fixings to go along with another partner of ours that's giving ham and pies," Alcime said.GL Homes is among the community partners supporting SPECTRA's Thanksgiving efforts.Sarah Alsofrom, vice president of community relations with GL Homes, said the company provided $5,000 for turkeys along with nonperishable food for Thanksgiving meals."We've given $5000 worth of turkeys so that people can have a happy Thanksgiving and all of these great canned items, non-perishable goods, all the trimmings, and we need more help from the community to provide more," Alsofrom said.More than 280 families are still waitingThe Thanksgiving distributions are helping hundreds of families, but Palm Beach County Housing Authority Executive Director and CEO Carol Jones-Gilbert said the need continues."We have, we've served families, but we have an additional 280 families on the waitlist," Jones-Gilbert said. "We serve more than 8000 people in Palm Beach County, so there's always a need, and so we're always looking for partners to collaborate with us."The need is particularly timely during Thanksgiving week, when the cost of preparing a holiday meal can add another expense for households already balancing food, utilities, childcare and other necessities.For SPECTRA, the goal extends beyond a single Thanksgiving meal. Jones-Gilbert said community partnerships and in-kind donations can help the Housing Authority address needs outside traditional housing assistance."Our ask is we're always looking for partners for in-kind donations to help us to not make sure, to make sure we not just provide housing, but that our families thrive," Jones-Gilbert said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. U2 is heading back to stadiums, and the rock band's newly announced North American tour will begin in Miami.Live Nation announced U2's Carnaval De Luz presents: The Greatest Show On Earth World Tour 2027 will kick off its North American leg at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens on Aug. 13, 2027.The tour will feature Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. and include 15 stadium shows across the United States and Canada.The announcement comes as U2 promotes its 16th studio album, "Carnaval De Luz," which was released Nov. 13. The 12-track album is the band's first new release in nine years.The North American dates follow previously announced shows in Latin America and Europe. According to Live Nation, initial concerts in Mexico City, São Paulo and Buenos Aires sold out, prompting additional dates.The 2027 tour will mark U2's first stadium outing since The Joshua Tree Tour concluded in Mumbai in December 2019. Fans must register by Sunday, Nov. 29, at 9 p.m. ET to participate. No presale code is required because access will be linked to the fan's account.Remaining tickets will go on sale to the general public Friday, Dec. 4, at 10 a.m. through U2.com.

The 19-year-old son of a Florida county commissioner was shot and killed while camping in Santa Rosa County on Sunday.Carey Washington Vinson, a history major at Florida State University, was the son of Joe Vinson, who was recently elected to the Escambia County Commission.The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office said investigators are working to identify those involved in Carey's death and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. No arrests have been announced.In an emotional Facebook post Tuesday, Joe Vinson remembered his son, whom the family affectionately called "Wash," and pushed back against suggestions that his death was an accident."This was not a freak hunting accident — not someone firing carelessly in the dark," Vinson wrote. "It was not a 'stray bullet' that killed our Wash."According to Vinson, the family understands that someone stood on the opposite bank of the river and pointed a gun toward the occupied sandbar campground.He said the shooters were close enough to see the campfire and hear people talking."They fired shot after shot with malicious intent," Vinson wrote, alleging that the shooters fired another round after campers screamed for them to stop, then laughed as they drove away.Those details reflect the family's understanding of the shooting. The sheriff's office has not publicly confirmed that account in the statement provided.Vinson remembered his son as a thoughtful, outgoing young man who loved history, music and adventure. Carey was an excellent debater, played piano and guitar, and had recently been accepted into a summer study-abroad program in Valencia."Most of all, he had a tender and loving heart — for his friends and family, for his girlfriend, for animals, for the marginalized," Vinson wrote. "He was quick to laugh and easy to love.""I can't believe I'll never feel his hugs again, or hear him bickering with his siblings," his father wrote. "I can't believe any of this."The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is asking anyone who witnessed suspicious activity near Deaton Bridge Road and Boat Ramp Road, or who has information that could help identify those involved, to contact investigators.Anyone with information can call the sheriff's office at 850-983-1190, Option 1.Anonymous tips can also be submitted to Santa Rosa Crime Stoppers at 850-437-STOP (7867) or through the P3 Tips mobile app."I know it won't bring back Wash, but I would sleep better knowing they can't hurt anyone else," Vinson wrote.

A homeowner in Palm City helped foil an attempted home invasion that occurred at the Evergreen Club. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says on Tuesday morning a homeowner on SW Bimini Circle heard a noise outside of their home, leading them to call 911 and interrupting the home invasion. When deputies arrived at the scene, the four suspects, three men and a teenager from Jacksonville, scattered into the neighborhood. The sheriff's office says deputies set up a perimeter around the neighborhood with help from its aviation team, K-9 unit, and the Stuart Police Department. K9's were able to track down all four suspects hiding in separate locations throughout the community. The sheriff's office says at least one of the suspects was armed. Further investigation revealed that the suspects parked along the canal and walked into the neighborhood to target the home. The sheriff's office says during the apprehension they uncovered masks, a firearm and gloves. The suspects were identified as: Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 21 Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21 Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21 Teenage boy, 16 All four were charged with an attempted home invasion and were taken to the Martin County Jail. Wise faces an additional charge of grand theft and possession of a firearm. See also: Boca Raton police arrest man after reported assault on El Rio Trail The agency is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. Anyone who finds anything missing should call the sheriff’s office at 772-220-7060. This is a developing news story.

Small Business Saturday is just around the corner, and downtown Fort Pierce business owners are urging shoppers to support local stores as the holiday shopping season begins. Small Business Saturday was created by American Express in 2010 to get more customers through the doors of small businesses the Saturday after Thanksgiving. Small business owners in Fort Pierce are hoping you will shop small Saturday, and they're hoping you'll do it right here. The Executive Director of Main Street Fort Pierce, Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti and volunteers have been reminding business owners about the significance of Small Business Saturday. "Thank you so much for participating with Shop Small with us. Thank you, we appreciate it," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Juline Gurney, the owner of I Am Activeware, reflected on last year’s event, saying, "Last year I feel like there was a lot of new businesses, including myself, and downtown is a great spot to be. I had many visitors, to be exact 19 visitors that day, and my sales paid my rent that month." Newcomer, Kim Brant, the owner of Sunshine State of Mind Boutique, is excited about this weekend's event. "Last year I feel like there was a lot of new businesses, including myself, and downtown is a great spot to be," Brant said. This is year number nine for Beryl Muise, the owner of Notions Potions candles and more. Muise says Small Business Saturday is the most important shopping day of the year. "So that is our busiest shopping day of the entire year for us. And with that, retail has a very short window to make their money for the year, and so Shop Small Saturday kicks that off," Muise said. Main Street Fort Pierce is hosting the event, and organizers emphasized the importance of supporting local businesses, especially as some struggle to stock their shelves. "For a small business, putting the merchandise on the shelf is the equivalent of putting food on the table. They can't be separated," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Shopping locally also benefits the community, organizers said. "And remember when you spend a dollar in a small business, $0.68 of that dollar stays in your community. That gives the ability for your money to do more, spread wider, and have a longer impact," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Shoppers will also have the chance to participate in a raffle to win hundreds of dollars in gift cards. The shops in downtown Fort Pierce will open at 10 a.m. Saturday, and raffle tickets must be submitted by 5:30 p.m. The drawing will take place at 6 p.m. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

Cars were still getting through when CBS12 News reached one of the spots Port St. Lucie police had flagged for high water Thursday. Water pooled along Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and nearby driveways were dry. Earlier, water had made a lane impassable in two places on Village Parkway, and crews were pumping it off Tradition Parkway. Two weeks ago, floodwater stranded drivers across the city. Near Oak Hammock K 8, video showed a mother and daughter wading through chest-deep water. One location in Port St. Lucie recorded 16.7 inches of rain over 60 hours during that storm. Where police reported flooding Port St. Lucie Boulevard: Crews were putting up barricades at McCorkle Avenue, at Alcantara Boulevard and along the stretch from Southwest Liberty Drive to Firestone. Northbound Village Parkway: The right lane was impassable south of the fire station and south of Discovery Way. Water was spreading into a second lane near Discovery Way. Tradition Parkway east of Hazel Drive: Crews were pumping water off the road after the outside lanes flooded in both directions. Police said more closures could be needed as rain continued. The Florida Department of Transportation also had overnight closures scheduled this week on Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Southwest Fisherman and Southwest Liberty avenues for drainage work tied to a widening project. Where to fill sandbags St. Lucie County says sand is still available while supplies last at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds’ west parking lot, 15601 W. Midway Road in Fort Pierce. The Lawnwood Stadium site has run out. The fairgrounds site is self-service. Bring a shovel and plan to fill your own bags. The county has a limited supply of bags and encourages residents to bring their own. Residents in unincorporated St. Lucie County can report flooding that threatens homes, businesses or personal safety to flooding@stlucieco.gov. What was different this time Port St. Lucie crews started lowering water levels in stormwater basins Sunday to make room for more rain. They also cleared drains and checked canals and culverts. A lot of it just depends on how much rain you get at a given time, city spokesperson Scott Samples said. During the Nov. 1 3 storm, Samples said, rain came down so quickly that the drainage system needed longer to move it. This week, he said, less rain had fallen all at once. We’ve been fortunate that so far we haven’t had that kind of rain, he said. Samples said homeowners associations and community development districts manage drainage in parts of Tradition. The city helped pump water out of a neighborhood there after the first storm, he said. It’s really a very collective stormwater system. A flood watch remains in effect for St. Lucie County through 7 p.m. Friday. The National Weather Service issued a separate advisory Thursday morning after radar and gauges indicated 2 to 4 inches had fallen across parts of northeastern St. Lucie County and eastern Indian River County. forecast.weather.gov See also: Who’s responsible for improving drainage after St. Lucie County’s historic flooding? St. Lucie County schools and district offices are closed Wednesday as families prepare for more heavy rain, two weeks after flooding left roads underwater and damaged homes. All aftercare programs, after-school activities and athletic events scheduled for Wednesday are also canceled. See also: Flood risk continues for the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches through Friday evening The school district said forecasts show the potential for significant rainfall and localized flooding. With the ground already saturated, the district said closing schools was the cautious choice for students, families and employees. Officials are monitoring rainfall, flooding, road closures and access to schools, bus stops and transportation routes. The district plans to announce Wednesday evening whether schools will reopen Thursday. Across the Treasure Coast, some residents are filling sandbags to protect their homes. Others are stocking up on groceries and preparing to stay home if roads flood again. Leo Vargas of Port St. Lucie says floodwater rose to his knees two weeks ago, damaging his garage and guitars. He filled sandbags at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds and is adding more around his home. We had a lot of water go into the garage and we just got over the fact that it stopped smelling like mold in there, Vargas said. And then here we go again with this inclement weather. St. Lucie County set up self-service sand distribution sites at the county fairgrounds in Fort Pierce and the Lawnwood Stadium parking lot. Residents need to bring their own bags and shovels and fill the bags themselves. Sand is available while supplies last. By 6 p.m. Tuesday, the two truckloads at Lawnwood Stadium were nearly gone. Glen Ferlance was out for a morning walk Wednesday morning when he spoke with CBS12. He said the flooding two weeks ago kept him from reaching his children. I could not get to cross over to go and see my kids, Ferlance said. I had to park in the um the plaza here and just look on. Ferlance said he lives in Port St. Lucie and he’s preparing for more rain, but hopes the flooding won’t be as severe this time. I just hope that is not too bad like last time. Yes, I’m prepared, he said. I’m going to get something to eat, and I’m running back home in my bed to watch TV and relax until all this is over. He also said he’s glad St. Lucie County schools are closed. I just thank God they’re not school today, so the kids then should be more safe at home, he said. Some residents are also stocking up on food and supplies. Shoppers told CBS12 they’re preparing to stay home if roads flood again. The district said updates about school operations will be shared on its website and social media channels. Martin County canceled after-school activities. Schools in Indian River and Okeechobee counties remain open as of Wednesday morning. Palm Beach County schools and offices are open Wednesday, but the district canceled all after-school activities and athletics because of the afternoon forecast. Aftercare families must pick up their children by 4 p.m., the district said.
