cards.headline: Indian River County extends emergency through Nov. 23 as more rain threatens flooding
cards.teaser: Crews cleaned swales and inspected drainage systems as officials warned that saturated ground could leave more neighborhoods vulnerable to flooding.
cards.body:
Indian River County has extended its local state of emergency through Nov. 23 as crews prepare drainage systems for more rain. Emergency management officials warned that saturated ground could lead to flooding in areas that did not flood during the last storm. Crews cleaned swales and inspected drainage systems across the county as officials prepared for the possibility of more flooding.

Officials are closely monitoring flood-prone communities, including Heritage Plantation, Whispering Palms, and areas near Highland Drive. Ryan Lloyd, Deputy Director and Emergency Management Chief for the Indian River County Department of Emergency Services, urged residents countywide to prepare for possible flooding. “There could be areas that flood that we're not expecting per se or that necessarily flooded in the past,” Lloyd said.

Lloyd also asked residents to avoid driving through flooded neighborhoods to look at the damage. “We also ask our residents to please not do flood tours where they're going out just by standing and looking on at flooded neighborhoods, as they drive through those neighborhoods,” Lloyd said. “It can create waves that actually go into the houses, and it can make the flooding even worse for residents.”

Earlier this month, flooding left neighborhoods inundated, roads impassable and traffic disrupted. As of Tuesday, the county reported two properties destroyed and seven with major damage from the previous storm. Another 65 properties had minor damage, and 97 others were affected. The county's emergency information center is open for questions about the flood threat. Residents can call 772-226-4000 for assistance.

hero.headline: Boil-water notice continues for 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
A precautionary boil-water notice remains in effect for approximately 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie despite fully restored water service following a water main break near Glades Cut Off Road. City officials said the notice will remain in place until laboratory testing confirms the water is safe to drink.

The advisory affects customers in Tradition, Riverland, Western Grove, Wilson Grove, Southern Grove, Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano, as well as properties along Glades Cut Off Road. Residents should continue boiling water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and washing dishes until the city announces that the notice has been lifted.

A contractor working on a non-city construction project struck the 36-inch water main. Crews completed repairs Tuesday evening and began flushing the system. Water quality sampling is underway, city officials said. Because of the large number of customers affected, officials said the advisory could extend beyond the initial 48-hour timeframe.

For Marcus Rowe, a sudden drop in water pressure was the first sign of trouble. “I went to turn on the faucet, and the water pressure was low. I was like, 'what's going on'?” The Rowe family has been relying on bottled water and boiling water for daily needs while the advisory continues.

cards.headline: Rain worsens Milton damage at Port St. Lucie home, homeowner says
cards.teaser: Caryn McGregor says water is entering through her ceiling, windows and vents as she awaits state repair assistance. A repair assessment documents unrepaired Hurricane Milton damage.
cards.body:
Recent heavy rain is worsening unrepaired Hurricane Milton damage at Caryn McGregor’s Port St. Lucie home, she said, as she waits for state assistance to repair or replace it. Water continues entering through the ceiling, windows and vents more than two years after the storm.

McGregor said her roof was damaged when Milton struck Florida in October 2024. She initially contacted her insurance company but could not afford the deductible, she said, and later sought help through the state’s Rebuild Florida Housing Repair and Replacement Program.

A repair assessment lists Oct. 9, 2024, as the date of loss and Jan. 6, 2026, as the home’s inspection date. It documents unrepaired storm damage and notes that McGregor reported plumbing problems since the hurricane. The proposed work includes repairs involving ceilings, walls, plumbing, siding, appliances, drywall and doors.

McGregor has been using buckets and towels to manage the water entering her home. She said water has damaged her washer, dryer and dishwasher, and she worries that parts of the ceiling could collapse. “I can't even have my son living here because the ceiling, I'm scared of it falling on him and hurting him,” McGregor said. She also expressed concerns about water and mold.

McGregor said repairs remain unfinished and that she has been told the project is waiting on permits before work can move forward. “They were supposed to help,” she said. “However they were going to rebuild or replace it, they were supposed to do that.”

Recent rainfall has added to her concerns about the damage. “I want them to help us fix our house,” McGregor said. “They said they were going to.”

hero.headline: Teen arrested after Port St. Lucie hit-and-run critically injures scooter rider
hero.body:
An 18-year-old driver was arrested after police said he left the scene of a Port St. Lucie crosswalk crash that critically injured a 24-year-old woman riding an electric scooter. Police identified the driver as Tristan Sanchez-Chasmer and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The crash happened Monday morning near Southwest Gatlin Boulevard and Southwest Feather Terrace. Investigators said the woman was riding west on the sidewalk toward Southwest Rosser Boulevard. As she entered the crosswalk, a gray Chevrolet Tahoe driven by Sanchez-Chasmer struck her while making a left turn onto Southwest Feather Terrace, police said.

Police said Sanchez-Chasmer fled without stopping to render aid to the woman. The Traffic Homicide Investigations Unit identified him and located the vehicle during its investigation.

Investigators also learned that Sanchez-Chasmer had been playing “ding dong ditch” just before the crash, police said.

hero.headline: Indian River County extends emergency through Nov. 23 as more rain threatens flooding
hero.body:
Indian River County has extended its local state of emergency through Monday, Nov. 23, as officials prepare for heavy rain that could bring renewed flooding over the next 72 hours. Emergency management officials said saturated ground could leave areas vulnerable, including places that did not flood during the last storm.

Officials are closely monitoring flood-prone communities, including Heritage Plantation, Whispering Palms, and areas near Highland Drive. Ryan Lloyd, Deputy Director and Emergency Management Chief for the Indian River County Department of Emergency Services, urged residents countywide to prepare for potential flooding. “There could be areas that flood that we're not expecting per se or that necessarily flooded in the past,” Lloyd said.

Lloyd also asked residents to avoid driving through flooded neighborhoods to look at the damage, warning that those trips can worsen conditions for people living there. “It can create waves that actually go into the houses, and it can make the flooding even worse for residents.”

Crews spent the day cleaning swales and inspecting drainage systems across the county. Earlier this month, flooding left neighborhoods inundated, roads impassable and traffic disrupted. As of Tuesday, the county reported two properties destroyed and seven with major damage from the previous storm. Another 65 properties had minor damage, and 97 others were affected.

The county's emergency information center is open to answer questions about the flood threat. Residents can call 772-226-4000 for assistance.

hero.headline: Boil water notice continues for 21,000 western Port St. Lucie customers despite repairs
hero.body:
A precautionary boil water notice remains in effect for approximately 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie despite fully restored water service. City officials said testing requirements could keep the advisory in place beyond the initial 48-hour timeframe.

Water quality sampling is underway, and the notice will remain in effect until laboratory testing confirms the water is safe to drink. Officials said the large number of customers affected could extend the advisory.

The notice followed damage to a 36-inch water main near Glades Cut Off Road. A contractor working on a non-city construction project struck the main. Crews completed repairs Tuesday evening and began flushing the system.

The advisory affects customers in Tradition, Riverland, Western Grove, Wilson Grove, Southern Grove, Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano, along with properties along Glades Cut Off Road.

Residents are advised to continue boiling water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and washing dishes until the city announces that the notice has been lifted.

cards.headline: Free sandbag sites open in Fort Pierce, St. Lucie County ahead of heavy rain
cards.teaser: Residents can fill their own sandbags at four locations as public works crews clear drainage systems. Standing water from the last storm is adding to concerns.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce and St. Lucie County are offering free self-service sandbag sites as residents prepare for heavy rainfall this week, with some still facing standing water from the previous storm. County public works crews are inspecting swales and drainage systems, clearing them to address potential flooding.

The City of Fort Pierce is offering sand at Martin Luther King Jr. Dreamland Park and Jaycee Park. Both parks are open daily from dawn to dusk. Residents should bring their own bags and shovels. Residents have been filling sandbags at Dreamland Park to protect their homes.

St. Lucie County has also established self-service sandbag distribution points at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds West Parking Lot and Lawnwood Stadium Parking Lot. Residents must bring their own supplies and fill their own bags. Dickerson Infrastructure and Stewart Materials donated sand for the county sites. Residents can find updates about precautions at www.readystlucie.org or contact the Public Works Department for more information.

Lisa Powell, whose ditches remain full from the last storm, described her concern: “The water is just still standing there, up to the yard.” Recent flooding left parts of the county submerged and residents in the Creekside development trapped inside. Some used kayaks to navigate flooded streets, while others waded through the water.

Fredrick Reeves, whose home previously flooded, is using sandbags and mulch to try to block water from entering his house before the upcoming rain. During the earlier flooding, he put down clothes to soak up the water, but it continued flowing into the house. Reeves described the situation as “overwhelming.” Another resident whose crawlspace took on a foot of water was filling sandbags to cover the opening.
